title: Take a walk, bring back an idea
description: A short walk is a gentle way to unstick a stuck project. Arrive home with one idea, not ten.

body.heading: Moving helps thinking loosen
paragraphs: Many people notice that ideas arrive in the shower, on a bus or halfway around the block. A change of scene and gentle movement seem to loosen thoughts that staring at the page only tightens.
You do not need a long hike. Ten or fifteen minutes around your own streets is enough, and you can leave the headphones out so your mind has room to wander.

body.heading: Set one small mission
paragraphs: Before you go, name the problem in one sentence: 'I need an ending for the story' or 'I need a colour for the poster'. Then stop trying to solve it and just walk.
Carry a way to catch whatever surfaces: a notes app, a scrap of paper, a voice memo. Aim to bring back one usable idea. If none comes, you still had a walk, which is its own small win.

takeaway: Name the problem, take the walk, and catch one idea on the way home.
